newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle thin in light test - feedlot.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle thin in light test - feedlot.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle Wednesday traded in light "clean-up" activity following hefty sales on Tuesday, several feedlot sources said.
About 2,000 head sold in a limited test at $66.00 per cwt in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and about 1,500 in Kansas, they said.
Most of the small number of cattle that sold Wednesday reportedly were of lesser quality and would not yield as well as those that sold Tuesday at $67.00, they said.
"These were cattle that weren't the front end," one Kansas feedlot source said.
Several feedlot managers said they were able to sell out their showlists on Tuesday. Any cattle not sold that would likely have a high yield could still fetch $67.00, they said.
However, fed cattle prices could weaken regardless amid light demand from packers who have enough live inventories lined up for next week's short holiday slaughter schedule, the sources said.
Nearly all U.S. cattle slaughter plants will be closed on Monday in observance of the Memorial Day holiday.
Beef demand also was seen light immediately following the holiday, which could mute packer buying interest, they said.
